highlight.title: Cloud Run Instances and Worker Pools Transform Serverless
highlight.summary: Google Cloud announced Cloud Run instances—direct access to the underlying primitive without opinionated service abstractions—enabling long-running background agents. Coupled with worker pools for pull-based workloads and CREMA (Cloud Run External Metrics Autoscaler), this marks a shift toward more flexible serverless patterns for AI and queue-processing workloads.

resources.title: Cloud Run's GPU Support and Billing Caps Go Live
resources.why_now: GPU support with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell is now in preview, while billing caps for cost control are coming soon. These features address AI workload demands and FinOps concerns that dominate 2026 infrastructure decisions.

resources.title: GCP Cost Optimization: Spot VMs Save 91% But Need Interruption Planning
resources.why_now: With cloud bills growing 30% while traffic increases only 15%, teams need aggressive cost reduction. Spot VMs deliver up to 91% savings, but recent guidance emphasizes choosing less popular instance types to reduce interruption risk.

resources.title: IAM Agent Identity Goes GA for Agentic Enterprise Security
resources.why_now: As autonomous AI agents interact with sensitive data at machine speed, traditional IAM controls fall short. Agent Identity with Context-Aware Access for agents addresses the security paradigm shift that enterprises must implement now.

resources.title: Pub/Sub Lite Dies March 2026: Migration Planning Critical
resources.why_now: Pub/Sub Lite discontinuation on March 18, 2026 can substantially increase messaging costs without proper migration planning. Organizations need to evaluate retention policies and alternative architectures before the deadline.

claude_take: The serverless stack is evolving from simple request-response patterns to accommodate long-running agents and AI workloads, with Cloud Run instances representing the biggest architectural shift since containers. Meanwhile, cost optimization has become existential—not just nice-to-have—as evidenced by the aggressive push toward automation and FinOps tooling across every major cloud provider blog post this quarter.
